item.title: Viral video of jets buzzing DHL Stadium in Cape Town prompts aviation safety investigation
item.description: Viral video shows two Embraer E-Jets barely clearing DHL Stadium in South Africa before a Springboks vs. All Blacks rugby match in Cape Town.
item.content:encoded:
Last week, fans at a rugby match between South Africa and New Zealand got a show before the opening... uh... however it is that rugby matches start when a pair of Embraer E-Jets flew over the stadium.

Barely over the stadium.

Video of the moment quickly went viral, and it left a lot of people thinking, "Hey, that was very cool, but it seems like that may have been a little too low."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Well, despite some evidence that these low flyovers have happened before in South Africa, the stadium tower buzzing is now under investigation.

"It is therefore critical that we interrogate this past weekend’s events … to determine if there were any safety concerns which warrant a review," The South African Civil Aviation Authority (SACAA) said in a statement, per the Associated Press.

The flyover came just before the start of a match in the "Rugby's Greatest Rivalry" series that pits the Springboks against the All Blacks in matches around the world. This one in particular was in Cape Town and featured the two Airlink-operated jets flying over the city's DHL Stadium.

The airline was reportedly set to do another flyover at a match in Soweto, but has dropped those plans.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

It's good to at least take a look at this because if they weren't supposed to be flying that low, something needs to be done... but, man, that was cool.

There's just something about a flyover. I see planes fly over my house all the time, but when I saw a B-2 bomber soar over the Freedom 250 Grand Prix recently, it was like reaching another state of technologically advanced, radar-avoiding nirvana.

So, while safety has to be the number one priority, let's make sure we never do away with the wonders of having jets fly over stadiums full of people.

item.title: 2028 Dem hopeful's longtime ally exposed for deep ties to CCP officials: 'Good friends'
item.description: Rep. Ro Khanna's, D-Calif. former senior advisor on foreign trade and economic development could be liability to a potential 2028 campaign due to his ties to CCP officials.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., has been floated as a potential 2028 Democratic contender for president, but his longtime ally and former senior advisor on foreign trade and economic development could be a liability due to his deep ties to Chinese Communist Party officials, a Fox News Digital investigation found.

Henry Yin is a longtime California businessman and political operative who Khanna has praised for his "leadership" and has called one of his "good friends" on Facebook. He was born in China, raised in Taiwan and then moved to the United States, where he has lived for several decades.

However, while living in California, Yin has been a major player helping China get a foothold in California over the last several decades through multiple roles, including serving as a member of the California Commission for Economic Development and founding a consulting firm that included multiple corporate clients with ties to Chinese Communist Party officials. 

A 2011 profile piece revealed that Yin "made his fortune selling used computer equipment to China" and had "done business in China for more than a quarter-century." The profile piece went on to say Yin has "good connections and a sense of [China's] business climate" and was "leading city trade delegations to China, which have contributed to several Chinese firms — most recently software company Trunkbow International — setting up offices in the city and helping city businessmen get a foothold in China."

SWALWELL RESIGNATION COLLIDES WITH CHINA-LINKED SCANDAL AS CRITICS DEMAND FILE RELEASE

"Henry has some sort of special skill-building relationships," one businessman said in the profile piece, praising Yin. "There’s a lot more government involvement in China, and you need relationships with local government officials."

In addition to his consulting business and several overseas trips to China, Yin has allegedly attended at least 10 events hosted by United Front groups, including the All-China Federation of Returned Overseas Chinese (ACFROC), according to China expert Jackie Deal, the president of Long Term Strategy Group, a defense research firm. Fox News Digital has extensively reported on the CCP's United Front and the threat it poses to U.S. institutions as the CCP gains influence in the United States.

In a Sept. 2019 Facebook post, Khanna announced that Yin, who was first appointed to the California Commission for Economic Development in 2010 by then- Republican Gov. Arnold Schwarzenegger and later reappointed to the position in 2015 by the succeeding Democratic Gov. Jerry Brown, would "serve as my Senior Advisor on Foreign Trade and Economic Development."  

"We discussed the importance of improving the US China relationship to cooperate on issues of climate change and medical research while protecting intellectual property and opening access to markets," Khanna continued. "I was particularly touched that Henry and the group had a birthday cake for me. It was wonderful celebrating with them!"

A few months later, in December of the same year, Khanna posted about Yin on Facebook again, writing, "Thank you Henry Yin for your leadership!" 

That same month, Yin invited Khanna to be his "honorable guest" for an event titled, "S.V. U.S.-China Trading Partners Concerned Group Dinner Meeting Agenda," which was sponsored by Yin's consulting firm, USA-China-Link. A review of the event's presentations showed the attendees were slated to talk about an array of topics, including China investments, technology and business asset management, among other topics. Khanna was slated to discuss intellectual property.

ELITE US COLLEGES LINKED TO CHINESE SURVEILLANCE LABS DRIVING UYGHUR ‘GENOCIDE,’ STUDY WARNS

In Feb. 2020, Khanna posted another photo of himself having dinner with Yin, who he referred to as one of his "good friends." In the post, Khanna decried that "Chinese Americans are feeling they are being stereotyped as the symbols for the coronavirus." 

"This is a time to embrace our Chinese American neighbors and friends and continue to frequent Chinese-American stores, restaurants and shopping centers." 

On Yin's LinkedIn profile, which still includes the senior advisor title with Khanna's office, he includes over a dozen slides detailing his consulting business, USA-China-Link, and showcasing his business acumen in China, which was featured in several profile pieces in Chinese state media. One of the slides says his firm "specialized in high-tech and green tech" and helped China do business in California and vice versa. Other slides show a list of his Chinese clients and a slide that called him an "Official Commerce Rep in US for the Province of Fujian, China."

Another slide shows a photo of Yin at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing in 2009 for the China National Day Banquet, where he calls himself a "VIP" in the caption. According to reports on the event, the banquet included several senior-level CCP officials in attendance, including then-Chinese President Hu Jintao and his successor Xi Jinping, the former third-ranking member of the CCP's Politburo Standing Committee, Wen Jiabao, among other top officials.

A spokesperson for Khanna, who is a member of the House Select Committee on the CCP, told Fox News Digital earlier this year that "Henry Yin has never been employed by Rep. Khanna" and "he doesn’t serve in any role in his office or campaign." When asked Wednesday whether his office stands by the quote, Khanna's office did not immediately respond. Despite the previous denial, Khanna and Yin were pictured sitting beside each other earlier this year at an event.

In Feb. 2026, Khanna posted a photo showing him sitting beside Yin at a political action committee meeting in Sunnyvale, California. Khanna wrote he was "honored to be back in the district, hearing directly from Chinese American community leaders."

Yin has made several trips abroad to China over the last decade, including a July trip where he led a delegation to Guangzhou to meet with Zhu Xiaojun, the Department of Commerce of Guangdong Province's deputy director, which is a CCP-controlled position. A Chinese report on the trip said the two sides collaborated on two-way trade between California and the Guangdong province. Two months before the event, Yin attended the 2026 China-California Economic and Trade Forum, which was hosted by the Chinese Consulate in Los Angeles and included multiple CCP officials in attendance.

He also accompanied California Gov. Gavin Newsom in late 2023 for a delegation, where he served as an advisor, according to another Chinese media report. During the trip, Newsom would meet with top CCP officials, including Chinese President Xi Jinping and Wang Yi, who has been a CCP member since 1981 and is currently serving as a "Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, Director of the Office of the Central Commission for Foreign Affairs, and Minister of Foreign Affairs. Newsom also met with Han Zheng, China's vice president.

A Fox News Digital review of Yin's Facebook account also unearthed other China trips he made, including Chinese delegations he has helped host in California. In 2014, Yin signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) between the California Green Tech Center and China Venture Capital Association, which appeared to be one of his firm's clients. Other posts show multiple China visits, including the 2015 "China South Asia Expo," which featured a speech from the now-former Chinese Vice President Li Yuanchao. A 2019 post highlights another China trip he took, which he called "fruitful" and included over a dozen photos of Chinese officials he met with. One of the photos included the names of Chinese and American companies where he was facilitating trade projects. 

ELITE US COLLEGES LINKED TO CHINESE SURVEILLANCE LABS DRIVING UYGHUR ‘GENOCIDE,’ STUDY WARNS

A Fox News Digital investigation also unearthed a 2013 photo that appears to show Christine Fang—the Chinese spy at the center of the scandal involving disgraced former Rep. Eric Swalwell—alongside key political figures. Posing together at a public gathering, Fang stood behind then-Chinese Consul General to San Francisco Gao Zhansheng and top leaders from the Asian Pacific Islander American Public Affairs Association (APAPA), including Yin.

A recently declassified FBI report on Swalwell's ties to Fang Fang revealed that a "prominent businessman in the Bay Area" tied to APAPA introduced Swalwell to Fang Fang. While Fox News Digital could not confirm whether the redacted section of the FBI report was referring to Yin, or potentially his brother, C.C., who founded APAPA and opened up several McDonald's franchises, Axios previously quoted Yin saying that Fang Fang was "very active" with the APAPA Bay Area chapter and remembered seeing her at several events.

The photo was originally shared on Facebook in February 2013 by the late Don Sun, a prominent California civic leader and tech executive who passed away in 2024. In the photo caption, Sun wrote that the Yin family and APAPA had thrown a farewell dinner for the Chinese consul at San Francisco’s Embarcadero Center. Sun said the photo depicts the consul and "all my friends at APAPA."

UNEARTHED PHOTO OF SWALWELL MEETING WITH TOP CCP OFFICIAL RAISES ALARM BELLS: 'VERY DISTURBING'

An APAPA spokesperson confirmed that Yin is a current member of the group's board. The spokesperson wrote in an emailed statement earlier this year that the photo "appears to reflect a private gathering and does not represent APAPA programming, partnerships, or operations." They emphasized that attendance by individual members of APAPA at events "does not reflect organizational positions, affiliations, or activities beyond that context."

"Public officials should strongly scrutinize any APAPA efforts that align with CCP objectives, including the CCP influence operations to prevent data center construction across America," Michael Lucci, the CEO of State Armor, a nonprofit countering CCP threats, told the New York Post.

"APAPA does not have documentation to substantiate the characterization in Mr. Sun’s post that the dinner was ‘co-hosted’ by APAPA, and we cannot validate third party descriptions of the event based on a photo and a social media caption," the spokesperson said, adding, "Individuals may attend events in a personal capacity, and such attendance should not be construed as an organizational activity or endorsement."

The spokesperson also noted that "APAPA has no records indicating that he [Yin] has served as a senior advisor to Rep. Khanna" despite an APAPA press release from January 2022 announcing Yin joining the group's national governing board and states that he "has served as Senior Advisor to U.S. Representative Ro Khanna, who represents the South Bay Area." 

Pressed by Fox News Digital on this, the APAPA spokesperson said, "The current APAPA headquarters leadership and team had no knowledge of, and do not maintain any records confirming, Mr. Henry Yin serving as a senior advisor to Rep. Khanna. APAPA does not oversee, verify, or maintain records related to an individual’s outside titles or roles with public officials."

They added that "With respect to historical references appearing on legacy APAPA web pages or posts, APAPA is in the process of reviewing and removing outdated or inaccurate content that does not reflect current leadership, governance, or verified records." They added that "questions regarding any past or current status with Rep. Khanna’s office should be directed to that office or to Mr. Yin directly."

Yin did not respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

item.title: Popular diet slashes liver fat by 67% while reversing prediabetes in some people
item.description: A keto diet reduced liver fat by roughly 67% and reversed prediabetes in half of participants, but the study's small sample size is a caveat.
item.content:encoded:
The keto diet may have surprising benefits for liver health, a new study suggested.

The research, published in the journal Cell Metabolism, studied 42 adults who had obesity, prediabetes and excess liver fat.

In a randomized clinical trial, the participants were assigned to three weight-loss diets – a low-carb ketogenic diet, a Mediterranean diet and a low-fat, mostly plant-based diet.

SECRET TO WEIGHT LOSS MAY BE HIDING IN YOUR GUT, NEW STUDY SUGGESTS

The keto diet’s calories consisted of about 4% carbohydrates and 73% fat, according to the study. The Mediterranean diet provided about 50% of calories from carbohydrates and 35% from fat, while the low-fat diet provided about 70% of calories from carbohydrates and 15% from fat.

In all three groups, muscle insulin sensitivity improved by about 50%, helping the muscles take up blood sugar more efficiently.

Liver insulin sensitivity improved two to three times as much in the keto group as in the other diet groups.

Liver fat decreased by roughly 67% among people following the keto diet, compared with about 45% among those on the other diets. The reduction was linked to a decrease in the liver’s production of new fat.

Glucose and insulin measures also generally improved more in the keto group. About 50% of participants in that group no longer met the criteria for prediabetes by the end of the trial, compared with 29% of those following the Mediterranean diet and 7% of those on the low-fat diet.

ONE COMMON TYPE OF FAT MAY INCREASE DIABETES RISK, WHILE ANOTHER HELPS FIGHT IT

The study’s short duration and small sample size — about 14 people in each diet group — limit how broadly the findings can be applied to the general population, the researchers said.

The researchers concluded that, among people with obesity, prediabetes and excess liver fat, the composition of a weight-loss diet may influence certain metabolic outcomes beyond the effects of weight loss alone. The keto diet produced the greatest improvements in liver fat and liver insulin sensitivity in this small trial.

Registered dietitian nutritionist Ilana Muhlstein reflected on the study findings.

"I love more and more validation and recognition that calories are not equal," the California-based expert told Fox News Digital.

Muhlstein said people often reduce weight loss to "just a calorie deficit," but this study showed that differences in macronutrients were associated with different changes in health markers despite similar weight loss.

POPULAR DIET TREND COULD BOOST MENTAL HEALTH AMONG OLDER ADULTS, STUDY FINDS

Although weight loss occurred across all three groups, Muhlstein said the participants experienced different internal metabolic changes. The keto group showed a greater reduction in the liver’s production of new fat, along with metabolic changes consistent with greater fat burning.

Muhlstein explained that excess calories and metabolic dysfunction can cause fat to accumulate in the liver, even in people who do not drink alcohol.

She recommends that anyone with a fatty liver should consider transitioning to a lower carbohydrate diet.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Muhlstein said reducing carbohydrate intake may encourage the body to use more stored fat for energy.

The findings were notable because the keto group did not experience higher cholesterol or blood-fat measurements during the short study, the expert noted.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"This is a really interesting study for someone who has prediabetes, someone who had blood sugar irregularity, but maybe still something to be cautious of if someone has heart disease in the family or is at high risk of heart disease," she added.

Overall, Muhlstein said the findings suggest keto may be worth discussing as a short-term option for some people with obesity or prediabetes, particularly because the study found greater reductions in liver fat and higher rates of prediabetes remission — even though weight loss was similar across the three groups.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"Keto is not something I recommend for anyone long-term because of the high saturated fat, and usually it translates into a lower-fiber diet, which is not good for heart health," Muhlstein said.

"So potentially, it should be something used short-term early on for someone with prediabetes, and then they can transition into Mediterranean, which would be overall helpful for your heart, your brain and so much more."

item.title: GOP mail-in voting proposal could impact millions of Americans ahead of midterms
item.description: President Donald Trump's allies unveil a bill requiring mail-in ballots be received by Election Day, citing Florida's system as proof it works.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: The nationwide battle over how and when Americans can vote has hit Capitol Hill, with two allies of President Donald Trump unveiling a new proposal they say will help restore confidence in U.S. elections.

Rep. Laurel Lee, R-Fla., plans to introduce legislation on Thursday mandating that absentee and mail-in ballots are received by the relevant officials by the end of the day on Election Day. A corresponding bill is being led in the Senate by Sen. Ashley Moody, R-Fla.

"This is something that we've done in Florida for many years, and it's a really effective way of making sure that elections stay organized and that we have timely election results," Lee told Fox News Digital.

SUPREME COURT RULES ON MAIL-IN BALLOTS RECEIVED AFTER ELECTION DAY

Lee is Florida's former top elections official, having served as its secretary of state from 2019 until May 2022.

"Florida is proof-positive that this works, that it does not deny any voter the right to vote. Our job as elected officials or as elections officials throughout the states is just to make sure that voters know the deadlines, that they know the rules and tell them your ballot has to be received," Lee said. "They can do that just as easy as they can get it postmarked by Election Day."

TRUMP SCORES SUPREME COURT WIN ON MAIL-IN VOTING RESTRICTIONS BEFORE MIDTERMS

It follows an executive order Trump issued in March 2025 essentially setting an Election Day deadline for when mail-in ballots can be received.

If passed, the legislation could have a significant impact on millions of Americans, nearly a third of whom vote by mail.

FEDERAL JUDGE BLOCKS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION FROM RESTRICTING MAIL-IN BALLOTS AHEAD OF MIDTERMS

However, the topic of mail-in ballots has been a political lightning rod that's divided the GOP. Republicans in states where voting by mail is popular have expressed concern about changing the current system ahead of November.

But Lee argued her bill does not curb people's ability to vote by mail.

REPUBLICAN SAYS TRUMP'S TOP ELECTION PRIORITY 'DEAD' IN SENATE AS GOP FRACTURES AHEAD OF MIDTERMS

"One thing that's important to understand about this bill is that it doesn't limit voting by mail. It simply says that for states who allow mail voting, ballots must be received by Election Day," she said. "So it still keeps all of those options that states have chosen to implement on the table for them. It just creates a different deadline."

Meanwhile, a separate Trump order making significant changes to the mail-in voting system is currently at the center of a dramatic legal battle between the White House and over 20 states.

That order would create new hurdles for the U.S. Postal Service and other agencies to verify proof of citizenship before delivering ballots, as well as mandate the use of specific stationery denoting federal election mail.

Supporters of the rule have argued it's key to enhancing voter confidence in elections, while opponents have said it would do the opposite by sowing chaos in the current system.

item.title: Russia’s strikes near Moldova raise alarm over Putin’s plans for Europe’s eastern flank
item.description: President Sandu's national security advisor, Stanislav Secrieru, says Russia's strikes on Ukrainian-Moldovan border infrastructure aim to sever vital grain export corridors to European markets.
item.content:encoded:
As the war in neighboring Ukraine moves closer to its border, the former Soviet republic of Moldova, which just marked 35 years of independence, faces growing pressure from Russia. 

In exclusive comments to Fox News Digital, national security advisor to Moldova’s President Maia Sandu, Stanislav Secrieru, said Russia’s recent strikes against Ukrainian-Moldovan border infrastructure pose a major threat to Ukraine’s economy and access to European markets.

Secrieru told Fox News Digital that, "In August, Russia began striking Ukraine’s border infrastructure along the Moldovan frontier. With Ukrainian grain exports through the Black Sea ports under sustained attack, Moldova has become a transit route for that grain towards Romania’s ports — and the Moldovan government cut rail transit tariffs by half to keep it moving." 

US WARNS RUSSIAN-LINKED ACTORS SEEKING TO 'FOMENT MANUFACTURED INSURRECTION' IN EUROPEAN COUNTRY

These routes, Secrieru said, are a lifeline for Ukraine’s exports and for its economy. "Russia’s strikes are meant to sever them. Russia has also stepped-up violations of Moldova’s airspace in August, to intimidate us into withdrawing our support. Moldova stays the course. We will continue to provide civilian support to Ukraine and to keep the corridors that sustain its economy open," Secrieru told Fox News Digital.

President Maia Sandu reported five Russian drones violated its airspace just hours before the country celebrated its independence, in what the president called an attempt at "intimidation."

"We have repeatedly warned about the unacceptable risks posed by Russia’s war against Ukraine. Yet another Russian attack on Ukraine has once again resulted in violations of Moldova’s airspace," the foreign ministry posted on X. 

Secrieru told Fox News Digital that Russia violated Moldovan airspace on 17 occasions in August, the highest number of violations in a month since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy recently visited his Moldovan counterpart in Chișinău, taking part in Independence Day celebrations and emphasizing the shared struggle of Ukrainians and Moldovans in the face of the threat posed by neighboring Russia.

"Russia is doing a lot to ruin our lives in Ukraine, to ruin your lives in Moldova, and to make it as difficult as possible for Romania. This is the ‘Russian world.’ It spoils. It destroys. But we will win. I am sure," Zelenskyy told a large Independence Day gathering.

ZELENSKYY PRESSURES US AND EUROPE FOR MORE 'AIR DEFENSE' ASSISTANCE AMID ONGOING WAR WITH RUSSIA

RUSSIA USES AMMO DEPOT IN TRANSNISTRIA TO SMUGGLE WEAPONS ACROSS UKRAINIAN BORDERS

Both Moldova and Ukraine applied for EU membership on the same day, shortly after Russia’s invasion in 2022. Russia’s invasion and its destabilization efforts in Moldova complicate both countries' path forward to EU membership, a central goal of Putin’s Russia as Moscow has tried to stymie the countries of the former Soviet republic from moving closer to the West and EU institutions.

Russia’s new threats against its neighbors come on the heels of CIA Director John Ratcliffe’s surprise visit to Moscow, fueling speculation Russia intends to escalate conflict with NATO members, particularly the Baltic nations of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania.

Along with its kinetic actions in Ukraine and incursions into Moldova’s airspace, Moscow uses influence operations in the former Soviet space to aid pro-Russian actors and push pro-Russian points of view.

"Russia has been interfering in Moldova for years, and these latest reports fit the broader pattern of Moscow using hybrid warfare to test how far it can push Europe without triggering a serious response," Ivana Stradner, research fellow with the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told Fox News Digital.

Moldova remains a prime target for Russian influence operations over 30 years after declaring independence from the Soviet Union. Russia maintains around 1,500 troops in the breakaway territory of Transnistria, which split away from Moldova after the declaration of independence from the Soviet Union in 1991.

Stradner, who focuses on Russian disinformation campaigns, said Putin is counting on Western risk aversion and betting that if a country isn’t under the NATO umbrella, the West will decide it’s safer to look away.

"That’s exactly why Moldova matters. This could be a rehearsal for how Moscow tests the Baltics," Stradner warned.

The Baltic countries are taking notice of what’s happening in Moldova and there are growing fears that Russia may escalate the conflict beyond Ukraine.

Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna stated on X that while Estonia’s threat assessment has not changed, "Russia’s threat and possible provocations against NATO must be taken seriously." Other Baltic leaders including Latvia’s Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs reiterated that the threat of a Russian invasion remains low but warned of an increased risk of Russian actions.

Since independence, Moldova has set its sights on moving closer to the West, with recent elections and a referendum on becoming a member of the European Union gaining significant support.

item.title: Will the WNBA’s unserious, weekly sitcom destroy one of the greatest opportunities for women athletes?
item.description: Maine state Rep. Laurel Libby takes aim at the WNBA over its response to Sophie Cunningham and the debate over women’s sports.
item.content:encoded:
Since WNBA player Sophie Cunningham said that biological men should not compete in women’s sports or enter women’s locker rooms, the WNBA’s legitimacy as a women’s league and nearly everything it once stood for have gone up in flames.

And every ounce of that damage has been self-inflicted. Faced with visceral backlash from radical gender activists over Cunningham’s comment, league officials, team owners, and coaches have either sat back and watched the chaos engulf their league, too afraid to challenge the small but loud minority driving it, or kowtowed completely.

They are treating Cunningham, her supporters, and anyone else who defends women’s spaces as heretics deserving of insults, threats, and public humiliation.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

In doing so, the very people charged with protecting the integrity of women’s basketball have abandoned the women and girls whose opportunities their league exists to protect. They have taken the torch passed to them by generations of women who fought for the rights they benefited from and promptly handed it to activists determined to burn those protections down.

Predictably, a month of escalating absurdity has followed. Protests and counterprotests have erupted outside games, fans have been ordered to cover shirts acknowledging biological sex, a former NBA player wearing a shirt defining "woman" as "adult human female" was ejected from an arena, and two teenage girls holding a sign supporting Cunningham were berated by the co-owner of another WNBA team and told they were "f---ing insane." 

League leaders have even devoted a "task force" to deciding who exactly qualifies as a woman under the league’s collective bargaining agreement, which states that "only players who are women" may compete. To this day, they have yet to emerge with a clear definition or eligibility policy, because determining whether men belong in a women’s league is apparently too "complex and nuanced" for the leaders of the Women’s National Basketball Association. 

Cunningham’s own head coach, meanwhile, has claimed she is simply not "educated enough from a scientific standpoint" to take a position. Portland Fire head coach Alex Sarama said he had somehow never considered whether biological males should compete in women’s sports. He quickly added, of course, that he is "supportive of people from all communities," lest the mob turn on him next. 

Golden State Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase explicitly said women’s sports should include "trans women," meaning biological males, then somehow compared enforcing the biological distinction between men and women to discrimination she has faced over her Japanese-American heritage.

WNBA FOLLOWERS ENRAGED OVER THREE HEAD COACHES' COMMENTS ON PROTECTING WOMEN'S SPORTS IN TWO DAYS

Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve, seemingly the most eager to abandon the girls the WNBA was created to serve, used her team’s game against the Fever to make a political statement and wear a "Trans Kids Belong" shirt before denying in interviews that biological males entering girls’ locker rooms is a real concern.

She saved her most condescending response, however, for the two girls who were cursed at by the Seattle Storm co-owner for holding a sign reading "Thank you Sophie for speaking up for girls." According to Reeve, they are the ones who do not "understand" what the "real problems are." 

Really? One of those girls was Ahnaleigh Wilson, who lost an eighth-grade championship race to a biological male and competed against a male athlete four times this past cross-country season. If Reeve had experienced this humiliation when she herself was a student athlete in New Jersey, she’d likely feel very differently.

Countless other girls across the country share Wilson’s story. Here in Maine, Kessa Benner saw her dream of winning a state pole-vaulting championship "unfairly shattered" when a biological male who had competed in the boys’ division just a year before took first place in the girls’ event. 

When I, then a sitting member of the Maine House of Representatives, spoke up for Benner and girls with similar experiences, the male-led Democratic majority censured me and stripped me of my right to speak or vote until I apologized. Thankfully, the United States' Supreme Court intervened, and required my vote be counted. This same pattern that punishes girls and their defenders has now become entrenched at the professional level, the last place it should ever have taken hold.

Calling the WNBA’s response ignorance lets its leaders off far too easily. These officials, owners, and coaches know the difference between male and female athletes. They know why women’s basketball requires its own league and what happens to female players when that distinction is erased.

But acknowledging those facts would require them to stand up to the political, media, and institutional forces that now police every word spoken inside women’s sports. So, instead, they genuflect at the altar of a nonsensical political agenda and leave girls such as Wilson to pay the price.

The tragic irony is basketball is one sport where women can thrive professionally. Women play baseball, hockey and other sports but professional leagues in those endeavors are nowhere near as far along as the WNBA. 

But its descent from a serious professional sports league into an unserious, weekly sitcom crushes the hopes of both those who’ve worked so hard to get there, and the generations of girls in middle school, high school and college right now who hope one day to wear a WNBA uniform.

The league would not exist without generations of women who fought for female athletes to have their own opportunities to compete fairly. Its leaders inherited everything those women fought to create. By refusing to preserve those protections for the girls coming behind them, they are abandoning the league’s purpose and destroying its future.

Laurel Libby is a member of the Maine House of Representatives and founder of Lead Maine.

item.title: America’s quiet socialist takeover is spreading from town halls to classrooms
item.description: Low-turnout school board elections in 2026 could let DSA chapters reshape curriculum and budgets before communities realize the lasting consequences.
item.content:encoded:
The socialist experiment in America is no longer confined to Washington or deep-blue national politics. It is coming to city halls and school boards across the country, where low-turnout elections can transform ambitious ideology into binding budgets and classroom policy.

Local government often affects Americans’ everyday lives more directly than Washington, shaping taxes, municipal services, schools, policing, and housing. Americans should therefore pay close attention to the DSA’s steady advance into local government, where ideological commitments can collide with fiscal limits, practical administration, and community preferences.

On affordability, New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s municipal grocery plan illustrates how a policy marketed as relief for working families can shift costs and risks onto others. New York City has allocated $70 million toward five municipal grocery stores that will be operated by private firms under city requirements while selling a defined basket of essential goods at prices the city says will be 30% below typical retail prices. That "basket of goods" applies to selected produce, meat, seafood, pantry staples and other goods—not necessarily every product in the stores.

EXPERTS SCORCH MAMDANI'S GROCERY PLAN AS AN 'ILLUSION' THAT WILL HAVE TAXPAYERS FOOTING THE BILL

The Multicultural Business Coalition, which says it represents hundreds of small, immigrant- and minority-owned grocers, has filed two lawsuits. The group wants to stop the plan, arguing that independent grocers operating on narrow margins cannot fairly compete against taxpayer-supported stores. The litigation has not established that businesses will close, and the first municipal store is not expected to open until next year. Nevertheless, the dispute exposes a recurring flaw in government-centered economic policy. Making goods cheaper for one group can impose costs on another, including on family-owned businesses, their employees, and taxpayers.

A policy intended to protect the working class should not proceed without serious analysis of whether it could displace the middle-class entrepreneurs who have served these neighborhoods for decades.

NYC BUSINESS OWNERS REVOLT OVER MAMDANI’S GOVERNMENT-RUN GROCERY STORES: ‘DOOMED FOR DISASTER'

Local school boards present another opportunity for ideological politics because their decisions shape not only district budgets, but also what children are taught and which perspectives are treated as legitimate. When curriculum becomes a vehicle for political activism, academic achievement and intellectual diversity can become secondary.

The concern is not that schools should ignore controversial subjects or disadvantaged students. It is that consequential policies can be adopted without adequately examining educational evidence, fiscal tradeoffs, dissenting perspectives, or the preferences of local families. Because school-board elections frequently receive limited public attention, organized political groups can exercise influence disproportionate to their support in the broader community.

Los Angeles offers a prominent example. DSA-LA helped elect Karla Griego and Rocío Rivas to the Los Angeles Unified School District board and openly describes them as its "Socialists in Office." Its education agenda extends beyond conventional school policy to climate activism, immigration, LGBTQ+ protections, housing and labor policy, opposition to law enforcement, and anti-privatization efforts.

Such politicization risks infringing on parental rights while losing sight of education’s fundamental responsibilities—ensuring students can read, handle basic arithmetic, think critically, and acquire the skills necessary to navigate adulthood.

SOCIALISM MOVES INTO THE MAINSTREAM — THE WARNING SIGNS ARE ALL HERE

Nor are these candidacies confined to Los Angeles. "DSA-LA has endorsed and campaigned for Estefany Castañeda, Rivas and Griego, all of whom won seats on Southern California education boards; San Diego DSA backed Erin Evans; Greater Baltimore DSA supports Baltimore school-board member Ashley ‘Ash’ Esposito; and in the 2026 election, Twin Cities DSA is supporting candidate Christin Crabtree in Minneapolis." The national organization has also encouraged chapters to recruit and run school-board candidates. Taken together, these campaigns show a deliberate effort to extend democratic-socialist influence into education governance.

That makes transparency essential. School-board candidates should disclose organizational relationships, distinguish local educational needs from national political objectives, and explain how proposed policies will improve measurable student outcomes. Policymakers should likewise demand curriculum transparency, clear academic objectives, and credible evidence that new expenditures will improve outcomes such as literacy, followed by public reporting on whether those improvements materialize.

America’s civic character will not be transformed only in Congress or the White House. It can change one municipal budget, ordinance, labor agreement, and curriculum decision at a time.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

Democratic socialists have the same right as anyone else to participate in debates over inequality, housing, public services, and education. But no movement’s moral certainty should exempt its proposals from fiscal arithmetic, educational evidence, viewpoint diversity, or community consent.

The spread of DSA influence into local government is an effort to translate a national ideology into everyday governance, where the consequences become intensely personal. Spending commitments can raise taxes and crowd out essential services. Housing mandates can reshape neighborhoods. Public-safety experiments can affect whether residents feel secure. And ideological school policies can determine what children learn.

If this movement continues advancing through low-turnout elections and lightly scrutinized offices, Americans may discover their communities have been fundamentally changed only after the financial obligations and institutional policies have become difficult—and extraordinarily expensive—to reverse.

item.title: Trump’s Army secretary hunt takes shape as insiders float potential picks
item.description: Sean Parnell and Brian Mast are among names floated to replace Dan Driscoll as secretary of the Army after his reported clashes with Pete Hegseth.
item.content:encoded:
The hunt is on for the next secretary of the Army after Dan Driscoll submitted his resignation to the White House, opening a key leadership vacancy atop the nation’s largest military branch.

Driscoll said Wednesday will be his "last full day" serving as Army secretary, adding that serving in the role under President Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has been "the honor of a lifetime."

The next Army secretary will inherit a service undergoing a major transformation, with questions over readiness and the Army’s role as the conflict with Iran continues.

ARMY CUTS HELICOPTERS, PUSHES ‘AMAZON FOR WAR’ AS DRONE COMBAT RESHAPES MILITARY

Army Undersecretary Mike Obadal could serve as acting secretary once Driscoll’s departure is finalized. A former special operations officer and defense industry executive, Obadal has also taken on a more public-facing role, including speaking at conferences.

In the Trump administration, deputy officials have repeatedly stepped into top leadership roles after resignations or firings— including then-Navy Under Secretary Hung Cao becoming acting Navy secretary after John Phelan’s departure this year.

Sean Parnell, the Pentagon’s chief spokesman and a senior adviser to Hegseth, has emerged as one potential candidate, according to sources.

PENTAGON FIRES BACK AFTER MARK KELLY ACCUSES PETE HEGSETH OF TARGETING WOMEN AND BLACK MILITARY OFFICERS

"A lot of people inside [Office of the Secretary of War] want to see Sean Parnell become the next Secretary of the Army because they’ve worked alongside him and know what he brings to the table," a senior administration official told Fox News Digital.

Parnell, who serves as assistant to the secretary of War for Public Affairs, is a former United States Army captain whose platoon killed over 350 enemy fighters at the height of the Afghan War.

He unsuccessfully ran for the House in 2020 before launching a 2021 campaign for Pennsylvania’s open Senate seat, earning Trump’s endorsement. He later suspended his campaign amid domestic abuse allegations from his ex-wife, Laurie Snell, which he denied.

HEGSETH TURNS TABLES ON DEMS AS SPARKS FLY DURING HEARING CLASH: 'I PUT THIS ON YOU'

The senior administration official said Parnell understands the Pentagon and the problems inside from military experience paired with his work at the highest levels of the institution.

"He also understands the importance of working alongside General LeNeve, who has been carrying an enormous load to keep the Army moving, and giving the Army Staff the leadership and support they need to get it back on track," the official said, referring to the acting Army chief of staff.

A senior Pentagon official told Fox News Digital Parnell has "proven time and time again" that he is loyal to the president, citing that Parnell was present at his rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, where Trump was shot.

After the president was removed from the rally, Parnell stayed behind to help others get out, the senior Pentagon official said. Parnell returned with Trump to Butler three months after the assassination attempt.

"Their relationship goes back many, many, years at this point, and it's not just with the president. It's also very senior members of the White House that are with the President every single day," said the senior Pentagon official.

REPUBLICANS DEFY JOHNSON TO ADVANCE DEMOCRAT-BACKED UKRAINE AID

A third senior administration official told Fox News Digital that "Sean Parnell is 100% focused on the job he was appointed to by President Trump and Secretary Hegseth."

Florida Rep. Brian Mast may also be under consideration, a source with knowledge told Fox News Digital. The Trump-endorsed candidate serves as chairman of the House Committee on Foreign Affairs and previously served in the Army for 12 years.

Driscoll's exit comes after reportedly butting heads with Hegseth over concerns with the administration about the Army’s transformation and readiness, including his belief that Hegseth had hindered those efforts, Fox News Digital previously reported.

Parnell defended Hegseth’s leadership and said the department remains united behind his vision.

"Secretary Hegseth has been a transformative leader for the Department of War and, at President Trump’s direction, has ushered in a new era of Peace Through Strength. Standards and merit are back, our arsenal is stronger than ever before, and morale and recruitment across every service are at all-time highs," Parnell told Fox News Digital. "Secretary Hegseth has slashed bureaucracy, unleashed innovation, and delivered for our warfighters every step of the way."

"The entire Department is unified behind the Secretary’s vision and will continue working to put our warfighters and America first," he added.

Democrats and some Republican lawmakers unloaded on Trump and Hegseth over the changes in the Department of War.

North Carolina Republican Sen. Thom Tillis said Hegseth is "creating a leadership void at the top of our military ranks" while ranking Democrat on the Senate Armed Services Committee Jack Reed of Rhode Island said, "Hegseth is cultivating a culture where dissent is punished and competence is secondary to personal allegiance."

Navy Secretary John Phelan was ousted in April after reportedly clashing with Hegseth over shipbuilding and management.

FIRST ON FOX: TRUMP TO OPEN DIRECT LINE WITH MILITARY FAMILIES IN GROUND-UP READINESS PUSH

The White House directed Fox News Digital to DOW when asked for comment.

Fox News Digital reached out to Parnell, Mast, the Army and DOW for comment.

item.title: Gloria Steinem, feminist writer and activist, dead at 92
item.description: Feminist writer and activist Gloria Steinem has died at the age of 92, according to a statement posted on her Instagram page Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
Feminist writer and activist Gloria Steinem has died at the age of 92, according to a statement posted on her Instagram page Thursday.

"Yesterday, Gloria Steinem passed away peacefully at her home in New York City, surrounded by some of the many who loved her," the message read. "Gloria’s near-century on earth were years well-lived, and she continued working for equality until the very end."

"Gloria’s greatest gift was her ability to listen to others, to make others feel seen and heard. Her words, actions, and example gave people permission to be their truest selves. Gloria lived true to her independent spirit, always with curiosity and a great sense of humor," the statement continued.

The statement said Steinem "spent her recent years doing the two things she loved most: being in community with others and writing."

FLASHBACK: GLORIA STEINEM, NOBEL LAUREATES ARRIVE IN NORTH KOREA FOR PEACE MARCH ACROSS DEMILITARIZED ZONE

"Gloria loved the tradition of lighting signal fires on hills to light the way to the other side of the mountain. Lighting your own candle for Gloria makes you part of this global and celestial community circle," it added.

Born in Toledo, Ohio, in 1934, Steinem was a "founder of New York and Ms. magazines, and is the author of An Unexpected Life, The Truth Will Set You Free, But First It Will Piss You Off, My Life on the Road, Moving Beyond Words, Revolution from Within, and Outrageous Acts and Everyday Rebellions, in addition to many collections and essays," a biography on her website said.

"She co-founded the National Women’s Political Caucus, the Ms. Foundation for Women, the Free to Be Foundation, and the Women’s Media Center in the United States. As links to other countries, she helped found Equality Now, Donor Direct Action, and Direct Impact Africa," it added.

"Among many tributes and honors for her activism, in 2013 she was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom by President Barack Obama and in 2019, she received the Freedom Award from the National Civil Rights Museum," the biography continued, noting that "Gloria’s home is the heart of Gloria’s Foundation and has become renowned as a magnetic and life-changing center for feminist and activist thinkers from around the world."

Steinem "helped to found the Women's Action Alliance, a pioneering national information center that specialized in nonsexist, multiracial children's education, and the National Women's Political Caucus, a group that continues to work to advance the numbers of pro-equality women in elected and appointed office at a national and state level."

CELEBRITY ACTIVISTS WHO HAVE MADE A GLOBAL IMPACT

"She also co-founded the Women's Media Center in 2004. She was president and co-founder of Voters for Choice, a pro-choice political action committee for twenty-five years, then with the Planned Parenthood Action Fund when it merged with VFC for the 2004 elections," her website said.

Steinem married businessman and animal rights activist David Bale in September 2000.

Bale, the father of actor Christian Bale, died three years later from primary brain lymphoma. 

Steinem began her career as a journalist, notably one who reported, in 1963, on degrading conditions in Hugh Hefner’s Playboy empire, an undercover assignment she came to later regret, according to The Associated Press. She credited a meeting six years later, where women spoke out boldly in favor of abortion rights, with changing her career path.

"That speak-out was the beginning of activism for me," Steinem, who had undergone a secret illegal abortion herself at age 22, told the AP in an email in 2022, reflecting on the reversal of Roe v Wade. "Either our control over our own bodies is equal, regardless of sex or race, or we’re not living in a democracy."

Well into her 80s, Steinem was traveling the globe and speaking out on issues of importance to her. These included everything from genital mutilation to Korean reconciliation, but it was equality for women that took precedence.

"Being a feminist means that you see the world as whole instead of half," she once said. "It shouldn’t need a name, and one day it won’t."

In 2020, her life was the subject of a feature film, "The Glorias, A Life on The Road," based on her 2015 memoir and starring Julianne Moore.

And at 91, she collaborated on a picture book with Liberian peace activist and Nobel laureate Leymah Gbowee aimed at inspiring young people to change the world. "Rise, Girl, Rise: Our Sister-Friend Journey. Together for All" was published in February 2026.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Convicted predators face lifetime barrier under GOP lawmaker’s sweeping victim protection bill
item.description: Rep. Abe Hamadeh's, R-Ariz., Kayleigh's Law passed the House unanimously, requiring lifetime no-contact orders for convicted sex crime and violent felony offenders.
item.content:encoded:
An Arizona congressman is putting convicted predators on notice after the House unanimously backed a bill designed to prevent abusers from dragging their victims back into court years after their crimes.

"Protect the victim. Stop the predator. End the revolving door," Rep. Abe Hamadeh, R-Ariz., wrote on X after the House passed Kayleigh’s Law.

"When a predator is convicted, the court issues a lifetime no-contact order," he added. "Not until probation ends. Not until some judge decides he’s ‘moved on.’ For life."

Hamadeh told Fox News Digital that the legislation would deliver permanent protection to survivors of federal sex crimes and violent felonies by requiring courts to issue lifetime no-contact injunctions against convicted offenders.

TRUMP SIGNS HAWLEY MEASURE ADDING 200 CHILD EXPLOITATION INVESTIGATORS IN LARGEST CRACKDOWN EFFORT YET

"This is a common-sense type of bill where we’re supporting victims, and we’re prioritizing victims over criminals," Hamadeh said.

The Kayleigh’s Law Act of 2026, introduced by Hamadeh as H.R. 8481, passed the House with unanimous support Monday and now heads to the Senate.

The legislation is named after Kayleigh Kozak, an Arizona mother of five who was sexually abused as a child and later forced to return to court when her abuser sought to have a no-contact protection lifted.

Hamadeh said Kozak was hauled back into court 13 years after the abuse, and then had to return again when the man made another attempt the following year.

CALIFORNIA DEMS TRIGGER OUTRAGE AFTER SIDING WITH CONVICTED CHILD SEX OFFENDERS IN SHOCKING VOTE

"Can you imagine that you have to sit across the room from this man?" Hamadeh said. "That’s something a victim should never have to do."

The federal bill would prohibit an offender from contacting the victim directly or indirectly for the rest of the offender’s life, even after prison, probation or supervised release ends.

"When you abuse a child, or you sexually abuse a child, or if you commit a violent offense against them, you should never have to interact with that person ever in their lives," Hamadeh said.

Kozak’s fight for permanent protections grew out of her own experience with Joshua Jacobsen, a former teacher and soccer coach who pleaded guilty to sexual abuse and luring a minor for sexual exploitation. Kozak was 12 years old and one of his students when the abuse occurred, according to FOX 10 Phoenix.

NEWSOM-BACKED LAW LETS ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHILD RAPIST SEEK EARLY RELEASE AGAIN AS DA URGES 'STOP THE MADNESS'

Jacobsen was sentenced to six months in jail and lifetime probation. Nearly two decades later, he asked a Maricopa County judge to end that probation, arguing that his conduct over the previous 18 years showed he had reformed and was ready to "move on," the outlet reported.

Kozak returned to court to oppose his request.

"I am living proof that he is capable of sexually harming children," Kozak told the court. "He consciously chose to violate me, and he was convicted of committing a dangerous crime against a child while he was in a position of power."

Jacobsen’s effort ultimately failed. A Maricopa County judge denied his request in June, citing probation violations that included unauthorized contact with children and breaches of chaperone restrictions, according to Arizona’s Family.

Jacobsen remains on lifetime probation under the supervision of Maricopa County Adult Probation.

Kozak celebrated the House vote on X, saying the country was "one step closer" to giving victims of heinous crimes the permanent protection they deserve.

PREP SCHOOL TEACHER FILMED SEX WITH STUDENT SHE WAS TUTORING: ‘NOT MY BEST THINKING’

"No victim should ever have to endure the hell I had to walk through," she wrote. "When I discovered protection wasn’t permanent, I knew it had to change."

Versions of Kayleigh’s Law have passed in Arizona and Wisconsin. Hamadeh said more than 1,000 Arizona survivors secured lifetime protection during the state law’s first year.

In a statement announcing the House vote, Hamadeh’s office said the legislation aims to end the "legal tug-of-war" that forces survivors to repeatedly face their attackers in court to maintain basic protections.

"Victims should never again have to fill out another form, sit across from their abuser, or look over their shoulder because the sentence ran out, and the system shrugged," Hamadeh said in a statement following the vote.

The issue became personal for Hamadeh long before he entered Congress.

SENATOR TIM SHEEHY: SOFT-ON-CRIME JUDGES NEED CONSEQUENCES. THE JAIL ACT DELIVERS

He met Kozak about five years ago while running for Arizona attorney general. Years later, as he campaigned for Congress, the two met outside an In-N-Out Burger, where he made her a promise.

"I told Kayleigh, I said, ‘Kayleigh, the moment I get to Congress, it’s going to be one of my first bills that I get done,’" Hamadeh recalled.

Kozak and her children later joined Hamadeh at the Capitol as the House approved the legislation.

"Promise made, promise kept," Hamadeh said. "To actually see it done has been really wonderful."

Hamadeh, a former prosecutor and Army veteran, said Kozak transformed the trauma she endured into a campaign that could protect millions of other survivors.

NEW YORK BILLS COULD ABOLISH LIFE WITHOUT PAROLE FOR SERIAL KILLERS AND COP KILLERS, CRITICS WARN

"She’s turned this tragedy into something that’s an inspiration to so many," he said. "From the moment it happened, it’s always been personal to me."

Asked about defendants’ due process rights, Hamadeh noted that the restrictions would apply only after a conviction.

"This is not about the due process beforehand," he said. "They ultimately have to be found guilty of a crime."

Once an offender has been convicted and sentenced, Hamadeh argued, that person should not be allowed to contact the victim or repeatedly summon the survivor back to court.

"The victim shouldn’t be re-traumatized over and over again," he said. "At that point, they should have no ability to contact the victim ever in their lifetime."

AOC OFFERS RARE PRAISE TO LATE SEN GRAHAM FOR BACKING AI PORN BILL NOW STALLED IN HOUSE

Hamadeh said his time as a prosecutor showed him how emotionally punishing the court system can be for survivors forced to revisit deeply personal trauma.

"You have to relive that over and over again," he said.

"Justice is not complete if the victim still lives in fear," Hamadeh said. "Arizona already closed that gap. It is time the federal government did the same."

The legislation now faces the Senate, where Sen. Mike Lee, R-Utah, is leading the effort to move it forward, according to Hamadeh.

Hamadeh also credited Rep. Andy Biggs, R-Ariz., for helping move the measure through the House Judiciary Committee and urged Americans to call on senators to bring it to the floor.

"It passed unanimously in the House. It should pass unanimously in the Senate," Hamadeh said. "We should fix this once and for all and be able to save victims so much of this trauma and this terror."

Hamadeh said he hopes the bill reaches President Donald Trump’s desk before November.

"Call your senators," he said. "Ask them to bring up Kayleigh’s Law to the floor."

item.title: Why restaurant servers clear your plate before everyone finishes eating
item.description: An etiquette experts reveal the subtle body language cues that restaurant servers use to decide when to clear your plate and what diners often get wrong.
item.content:encoded:
Your empty dinner plate may be disappearing faster than etiquette says it should.

Traditional dining etiquette calls for restaurants to wait until everyone at a table has finished eating before clearing the plate. But many contemporary restaurants clear plates individually, creating an awkward question for diners: Is the server simply being attentive or are you being hurried out?

"Everyone at the table should be finished before all the plates are cleared," Jacqueline Whitmore, Florida-based founder of the Protocol School of Palm Beach, told Fox News Digital.

FED UP WITH SCREAMING KIDS AT DINNER? MORE AMERICANS SUPPORT ADULTS-ONLY DINING

Salar Sheik, who runs Savory Hospitality Restaurant Consulting in Los Angeles, said diners shouldn't automatically interpret a cleared plate as a hint to leave.

"Clearing a plate is not necessarily an attempt to rush the guest or turn the table," Sheik told Fox News Digital. "Often, the server is simply trying to keep the table tidy, maintain the flow of service and prepare for the next course."

Knowing exactly when to clear a plate, however, requires some finesse. 

Sheik said servers may look for cues such as a diner pushing a plate away, putting silverware together, sitting back from the table or looking around for the server when little or no food remains.

"We train the best service professionals to read the guest's body language, pace and overall energy to determine when it is appropriate to approach and clear a plate," Sheik said. "This is a subtle skill that only a small percentage of staff members truly master."

Getting it wrong can have exactly the effect diners suspect. Repeatedly hovering or trying to remove a plate while someone is still eating "can make the guest feel rushed and is a sign of poor service," Sheik said.

There are ways diners can signal whether they're finished, Whitmore said. Crossing a knife and fork on the plate indicates that a customer is still eating or resting, the etiquette expert said. Placing the utensils side by side at roughly the four-o'clock position indicates the meal is finished.

Sheik also points to silverware as a cue, though he cautions that such signals aren't completely universal. Customs can vary among countries and restaurants, he said.

The simplest solution may be to skip the guesswork altogether.

"If there is any doubt, the server should always ask, 'May I clear this for you?'" Sheik said.

While restaurants shouldn't make customers feel rushed, diners have responsibilities, too.

There is no universal limit on how long a party should occupy a table, Sheik said. It depends on factors including the restaurant, size of the party, waiting reservations and whether a specific dining time has been communicated, he said.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Whitmore's advice is similarly situational: "Read the room." 

If diners are lingering while a line of customers waits for a table, they should be mindful of those around them. If no one is waiting, she said, they should "go ahead and enjoy" themselves.

Ultimately, good service may depend less on decoding a diner's body language than on five simple words: "May I clear this for you?"

item.title: Penn State fraternity cocaine deals grew to kilo loads as pledges helped package drugs, witnesses testify
item.description: A former Delta Upsilon member testified he bought kilogram loads of cocaine from an alleged top supplier and sold drugs to Penn State fraternity members.
item.content:encoded:
BELLEFONTE, Pa. – A former Penn State fraternity member testified Wednesday that he bought and sold cocaine in quantities that grew from 100 grams to 1-kilogram loads as prosecutors detailed allegations of a drug operation running through fraternities near campus.

The testimony came during preliminary hearings at the Centre County Courthouse in Bellefonte, Pennsylvania, for Agostino Abbatiello, Mohammed Huraibi, Paul Robinson, Thomas Robinson and Robert Zanolla. The five defendants are among 14 people charged in the alleged Penn State drug operation.

Charging documents filed by the Pennsylvania attorney general’s office describe a hierarchy of alleged suppliers, distributors and fraternity members accused of weighing, packaging and delivering cocaine. Prosecutors allege the drugs were brought to State College from Philadelphia, New York and Long Island before being sold to Penn State students.

SUSPECT ARRESTED FOR ALLEGEDLY RUNNING METH LAB AT MICHIGAN STATE UNIVERSITY’S LARGEST ACADEMIC BUILDING

Thomas Robinson, a former Delta Upsilon fraternity member, testified that he and Huraibi began buying cocaine from Abbatiello in 2023. Robinson said their first purchase involved about 100 grams of cocaine for roughly $4,000.

Robinson testified that he stored the cocaine in his fraternity room, where he and Huraibi broke it down into half-gram bags and sold each one for about $80.

JEANINE PIRRO CALLS OUT 'DIRTBAGS' AFTER 14 CHARGED IN ALLEGED COCAINE RING OPERATING FEET FROM A SCHOOLYARD

He described additional purchases involving 250 grams, 500 grams and, eventually, about 1 kilogram of cocaine. Robinson testified that he began buying directly from Abbatiello through Snapchat after Huraibi stopped selling.

DOJ ANNOUNCES 81 ALLEGED GANG MEMBERS INDICTED AFTER PUERTO RICO DRUG TRAFFICKING TAKEDOWN

Robinson also testified that he purchased about 1 kilogram of cocaine from Abbatiello in July 2024, another kilogram in September and a third kilogram in November. He said he sold the drugs primarily to members of Penn State fraternities.

The complaints portray Abbatiello as a top-level supplier who allegedly used fraternity connections to distribute cocaine on campus. They also accuse him of supplying Robinson and other defendants.

THREE COLLEGE FRATS IN CROSSHAIRS AS HAZING CLAIMS OF BOOZE, BURNS AND HOSPITAL TRIPS SPARK CRACKDOWN: SCHOOL

The defense challenged Robinson’s credibility and memory, pointing out that he used cocaine while he was selling it. Robinson acknowledged that his drug use could have affected his recollection. He also testified that he was arrested in December 2024 and removed from the fraternity shortly afterward.

Huraibi, another former Delta Upsilon member, testified that he and Robinson discussed buying cocaine in bulk to resell. Huraibi said they purchased 100 grams from Abbatiello for about $4,000 in August 2023 and 250 grams for approximately $10,000 in November.

MIAMI SECRET SERVICE AGENT CHARGED IN NEAR-DEADLY FRATERNITY HAZING, OFFICIALS SAY

BORDER AGENTS UNCOVER $20M COCAINE STASH HIDDEN BENEATH TRUCK FLOORBOARDS IN MASSIVE BUST

Lars Zeepvat, a former Sigma Chi member, testified that Abbatiello’s alleged drug sales grew out of personal cocaine use. Zeepvat said Abbatiello later shifted toward selling cocaine for money and popularity.

Zeepvat also testified that Abbatiello sometimes kept cocaine in fraternity houses and apartments, where students gathered to use it. He described an alleged November 2024 delivery to Delta Upsilon involving a large brown bag that Abbatiello said contained about 400 grams of cocaine.

$290M COCAINE HAUL FOUND ‘SKILLFULLY CONCEALED’ IN MASSIVE BANANA SHIPMENT

The complaints also accuse Zeepvat and Zanolla of making trips to New York to obtain cocaine for Abbatiello. Zanolla allegedly helped transport the drugs back to the State College area.

In a separate hearing Wednesday, Ryan Matson testified that Paul Robinson helped retrieve a safe that had been hidden in the woods after Thomas Robinson’s arrest. Matson said Thomas wanted to keep drugs and money from being discovered during a potential raid.
